title: Effect of Topical Application of a Cream Containing Hydroalcoholic Extract of Rhus coriaria (Red Sumac) Seeds on the Severity of Episiotomy Pain and Wound Healing in Women Following Vaginal Delivery
index_summary: Study aim: To determine the effect of topical application of a cream containing hydroalcoholic extract of red sumac fruit seed on the severity of episiotomy pain and wound healing in women undergoing vaginal delivery Design: This is a randomized, controlled clinical trial with parallel groups and a triple-blind design, which will be conducted on 80 women undergoing vaginal delivery with episiotomy. Participants will be randomly allocated to the intervention and control groups using the block randomization method. Settings and conduct: Bahlool Hospital in Gonabad and Vali-e-Asr in Birjand Participants/Inclusion and exclusion criteria: Women aged 18–45 years with term singleton pregnancies who underwent uncomplicated vaginal delivery with a second-degree mediolateral episiotomy, were in good general health, provided informed consent to participate in the study, and had no diseases, pregnancy-related complications, or use of medications affecting wound healing were included in the study Intervention groups: In the intervention group, mothers will receive red sumac seed extract cream along with routine postpartum care. After episiotomy repair, they will be instructed to apply the cream twice daily to the wound site. Wound healing and pain will be assessed using the REEDA and Visual Analog Scales on postpartum days 1, 5, and 10. Mothers will also receive education on perineal care, daily records, and follow-up.In the control group, mothers will receive the same postpartum care and educational instructions provided to the intervention group; however, instead of the cream containing hydroalcoholic extract of red sumac seed, they will use a placebo cream. Main outcome variables: Episiotomy pain intensity and episiotomy wound healing

title: Evaluation the effectiveness of a Persian Medicine product containing anise and sumac (Pimpinella anisum & Rhus coriaria ) in the severity of anorexia in children: a randomized, triple-blind clinical trial compared with placebo : Isfahan Medical Centers , 2026
index_summary: Study aim: Overall Objective To determine the effectiveness of an oral Iranian traditional medicine-derived formulation containing anise and sumac on the severity of loss of appetite in children. Design: A controlled, randomized, parallel-group, triple-blind clinical trial was conducted in 70 patients. Block randomization was performed using random sequence generation software. Settings and conduct: Convenience sampling: Participants were recruited from Amin Hospital, Hazrat Zeynab Hospital, Foroughi Traditional Medicine Clinic, and private medical offices. Block randomization was used to assign participants to intervention and control groups. An independent individual prepared the randomization list, and medications were packaged according to the assigned codes. Participants/Inclusion and exclusion criteria: Inclusion Criteria Age 5–10 years. Daily energy intake ≤80% of the recommended intake, based on a 24-hour dietary recall completed with the mother. Parental informed consent. Exclusion Criteria Underlying disease based on medical history. Recent psychological stress, including depression or anxiety. Use of appetite-affecting or psychotropic medications within the previous 3 months. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to anise or sumac. Withdrawal Criteria Intolerable adverse effects related to the study medication. Use of appetite-affecting medications during the study. Failure to consume the syrup for 5 consecutive or 10 non-consecutive days. Withdrawal of consent at any time. New disease during the study that may affect appetite. Intervention groups: Group 1 : Participants will receive an oral syrup containing 500 mg of anise and sumac extracts in equal proportions (250 mg of each extract per 5 mL), administered orally at a dose of 5 mL twice daily for 8 weeks. Group 2 : Participants will receive an oral placebo syrup for 8 weeks. Main outcome variables: Severity of anorexia in children

Intervention group will consume three capsules containing sumac extract daily after meals for 12 weeks. placebo group will receive three identical capsules containing starch. participants will receive standard medical treatment for PCOS, consisting of 10 mg of Medroxyprogesterone daily for 10 days, starting from the 14th day of each menstrual cycle throughout the study period.
